# Reference

## Table of Contents

### Classes

* [`acme_kvstore`](#acme_kvstore): Global configuration of acme_kvstore: backend, areas, profiles and defaults.
* [`acme_kvstore::worker`](#acme_kvstore--worker): Prepares an ACME worker: acme.sh, the redis gem and an optional dedicated user.

### Defined types

* [`acme_kvstore::certificate`](#acme_kvstore--certificate): Declares an ACME certificate; issued and renewed only on its worker.
* [`acme_kvstore::deploy`](#acme_kvstore--deploy): Writes a certificate stored by acme_kvstore (and optionally key, chain, DH parameters) to files on this node.

### Resource types

* [`acme_kvstore_cert_data`](#acme_kvstore_cert_data): A purely read-only type for querying a certificate stored by acme_kvstore (and optionally its decrypted private key) from a Consul or Redis K
* [`acme_kvstore_certificate`](#acme_kvstore_certificate): Requests an ACME/Let's Encrypt certificate via acme.sh, renews it when required, and stores the certificate, chain and (optionally AES-256-GC

### Functions

#### Public Functions

* [`acme_kvstore::lookup_cert`](#acme_kvstore--lookup_cert): Looks up a certificate (and optionally its decrypted private key) stored by acme_kvstore, at catalog-compile time.
* [`acme_kvstore::request_cert`](#acme_kvstore--request_cert): Requests a certificate via acme.sh directly, without storing it in the KV store.

#### Private Functions

* `acme_kvstore::unwrap_if_sensitive`: Returns the plain value of a Sensitive[String], or the value unchanged if it is not Sensitive.

### Data types

* [`Acme_kvstore::Area`](#Acme_kvstore--Area): One entry of $acme_kvstore::areas.
* [`Acme_kvstore::Area_name`](#Acme_kvstore--Area_name): The name of an area, as CCI-UI accepts it: [a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,47}.
* [`Acme_kvstore::Ca_profile`](#Acme_kvstore--Ca_profile): One entry of $acme_kvstore::ca_profiles: an ACME CA with the account data needed to use it.
* [`Acme_kvstore::Certid`](#Acme_kvstore--Certid): A certificate ID: a single KV path segment (letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-'),
at most 120 characters as in CCI-UI.
* [`Acme_kvstore::Certificate_params`](#Acme_kvstore--Certificate_params): One entry of $acme_kvstore::certificates: the parameters of acme_kvstore::certificate.
* [`Acme_kvstore::Consul_config`](#Acme_kvstore--Consul_config): Connection details for the Consul backend ($acme_kvstore::consul).
* [`Acme_kvstore::Dh_param_size`](#Acme_kvstore--Dh_param_size): Size of the RFC 7919 ffdhe group used for DH parameters (see acme_kvstore::deploy).
* [`Acme_kvstore::Dns_profile`](#Acme_kvstore--Dns_profile): One entry of $acme_kvstore::dns_profiles: a DNS-01 challenge configuration.
* [`Acme_kvstore::Dnsapi_script`](#Acme_kvstore--Dnsapi_script): One entry of $acme_kvstore::dnsapi_scripts: a custom acme.sh DNS API script.
* [`Acme_kvstore::Domain`](#Acme_kvstore--Domain): A domain name for a certificate: an FQDN or a wildcard name ('*.example.com').
* [`Acme_kvstore::Redis_config`](#Acme_kvstore--Redis_config): Connection details for the Redis backend ($acme_kvstore::redis).
* [`Acme_kvstore::Secret`](#Acme_kvstore--Secret): A secret value, as a plain String (e.g. already protected by hiera-eyaml) or wrapped in Sensitive for redaction.

### <a name="acme_kvstore--deploy"></a>`acme_kvstore::deploy`

Fetches the certificate while the catalogue is compiled
(acme_kvstore::lookup_cert), so the compiler needs access to Consul/Redis.
Independent of the acme_kvstore class and the worker: pass backend,
backend_config, area and area_secret, or leave them undef to use the
acme_kvstore::* Hiera keys with the area's read-only credentials
(consul_read_token, redis_read_username/redis_read_password - never the
worker's read/write ones). The certificate's status decides: 'active'
writes the files, 'delete' removes them, anything else (including
'norollout') leaves them alone. See docs/lookup_cert.md.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `acme_kvstore::deploy` defined type:

* [`key_path`](#-acme_kvstore--deploy--key_path)

* [`fullchain_path`](#-acme_kvstore--deploy--fullchain_path)

Where to write certificate + chain (skipped with a warning if the issuer is not stored).

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-acme_kvstore--deploy--combined_path"></a>`combined_path`

Data type: `Optional[Stdlib::Absolutepath]`

Where to write certificate + chain + key (e.g. for HAProxy), with key_mode.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-acme_kvstore--deploy--dh_path"></a>`dh_path`

Data type: `Optional[Stdlib::Absolutepath]`

Where to write the DH parameters (RFC 7919 group).

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-acme_kvstore--deploy--chain_include_root"></a>`chain_include_root`

Data type: `Boolean`

Whether to append the self-signed root to chain_path, fullchain_path and
combined_path, for applications without a usable trust store. The root
must be stored in the area (CAs rarely deliver it; import it e.g. in CCI-UI).

Default value: `false`

##### <a name="-acme_kvstore--deploy--combined_include_dh"></a>`combined_include_dh`

Data type: `Boolean`

Whether to append the DH parameters to combined_path.

Default value: `false`

##### <a name="-acme_kvstore--deploy--dh_param_size"></a>`dh_param_size`

Data type: `Optional[Acme_kvstore::Dh_param_size]`

DH parameter size: 2048, 3072 or 4096.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-acme_kvstore--deploy--owner"></a>`owner`

Data type: `String[1]`

Owner of all files.

Default value: `'root'`

##### <a name="-acme_kvstore--deploy--group"></a>`group`

Data type: `String[1]`

Group of all files.

Default value: `'root'`

##### <a name="-acme_kvstore--deploy--cert_mode"></a>`cert_mode`

Data type: `Stdlib::Filemode`

Mode of files without the private key.

Default value: `'0644'`

##### <a name="-acme_kvstore--deploy--key_mode"></a>`key_mode`

Data type: `Stdlib::Filemode`

Mode of key_path and combined_path.

Default value: `'0600'`

##### <a name="-acme_kvstore--deploy--notify_services"></a>`notify_services`

Data type: `Array[String[1]]`

Services to notify when a file changes.

Default value: `[]`

##### <a name="-acme_kvstore--deploy--certid"></a>`certid`

Data type: `Acme_kvstore::Certid`

Certificate ID.

Default value: `$title`

##### <a name="-acme_kvstore--deploy--area"></a>`area`

Data type: `Optional[Acme_kvstore::Area_name]`

Area of the certificate.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-acme_kvstore--deploy--area_secret"></a>`area_secret`

Data type: `Optional[Acme_kvstore::Secret]`

The area's secret; only needed to write a key.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-acme_kvstore--deploy--backend"></a>`backend`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['consul', 'redis']]`

KV backend.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-acme_kvstore--deploy--backend_config"></a>`backend_config`

Data type: `Optional[Hash]`

Connection details including 'prefix' and credentials; used as given.

Default value: `undef`

## Resource types

### <a name="acme_kvstore_cert_data"></a>`acme_kvstore_cert_data`

A purely read-only type for querying a certificate stored by
acme_kvstore (and optionally its decrypted private key) from a Consul
or Redis KV store on the target system.

This type never modifies data in the KV store; all properties are
read-only (insync? always returns true, so there is never a 'change'
event). It is useful, for example, for custom functions/facts that need
to process certificate data from the KV store without the module
itself being responsible for that (see docs/consul.md and docs/redis.md).

The pem/has_key/private_key properties are only populated when the
certificate's status is "active"; for any other status they stay
undef, and the certificate/key documents are not even read from the KV
store. See docs/lookup_cert.md for the compile-time equivalent of this
type (acme_kvstore::lookup_cert), intended for use on the Puppet server.

#### Examples

##### Read an active certificate and its key on the consumer node

```puppet
acme_kvstore_cert_data { 'shop-example-com':
  provider       => 'consul',
  area           => 'web',
  backend_config => { 'url' => 'https://consul.example.com:8501', 'prefix' => 'acme' },
  decrypt_key    => true,
  area_secret    => $area_secret,
}
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `acme_kvstore_cert_data` type.

##### `active_version`

Currently active version number.

##### `chain`

PEM-encoded issuer chain without self-signed roots, built from the issuer entries (undef if the issuer is not stored).

##### `chain_error`

Why the search for the issuer failed, if it did (e.g. a Redis user without +scan).

##### `chain_missing`

Whether the certificate's issuer is not stored in the area.

##### `fullchain`

PEM-encoded certificate + chain (undef if the issuer is not stored).

##### `has_key`

Whether a private key is stored.

##### `latest_version`

Most recently written version number.

##### `pem`

PEM-encoded certificate (without chain).

##### `private_key`

Decrypted private key (only when decrypt_key => true).

##### `root`

PEM-encoded self-signed root of the chain, if it is among the issuers found (never part of chain/fullchain).

##### `status`

One of 'active', 'norollout' or 'delete'.

##### `updated_at`

Timestamp of the last change (ISO 8601).

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `acme_kvstore_cert_data` type.

* [`area`](#-acme_kvstore_cert_data--area)
* [`area_secret`](#-acme_kvstore_cert_data--area_secret)
* [`backend_config`](#-acme_kvstore_cert_data--backend_config)
* [`certid`](#-acme_kvstore_cert_data--certid)
* [`decrypt_key`](#-acme_kvstore_cert_data--decrypt_key)
* [`include_chain`](#-acme_kvstore_cert_data--include_chain)
* [`prefix`](#-acme_kvstore_cert_data--prefix)
* [`provider`](#-acme_kvstore_cert_data--provider)

##### <a name="-acme_kvstore_cert_data--area"></a>`area`

Logical area of the certificate.

##### <a name="-acme_kvstore_cert_data--area_secret"></a>`area_secret`

Area secret, only required when decrypt_key => true.

##### <a name="-acme_kvstore_cert_data--backend_config"></a>`backend_config`

Fully resolved backend connection details (Hash), including "prefix".

##### <a name="-acme_kvstore_cert_data--certid"></a>`certid`

Certificate ID, as assigned when the certificate was created with acme_kvstore_certificate.

##### <a name="-acme_kvstore_cert_data--decrypt_key"></a>`decrypt_key`

Valid values: `true`, `false`

Whether the private key should be decrypted and exposed via the private_key property.

Default value: `false`

##### <a name="-acme_kvstore_cert_data--include_chain"></a>`include_chain`

Valid values: `true`, `false`

Whether to build the chain, fullchain and root properties; it can cost a read of all certificates of the area.

Default value: `false`

##### <a name="-acme_kvstore_cert_data--prefix"></a>`prefix`

Overrides the global KV prefix for this query.

##### <a name="-acme_kvstore_cert_data--provider"></a>`provider`

The specific backend to use for this `acme_kvstore_cert_data` resource. You will seldom need to specify this --- Puppet
will usually discover the appropriate provider for your platform.

### <a name="acme_kvstore_certificate"></a>`acme_kvstore_certificate`

Requests an ACME/Let's Encrypt certificate via acme.sh, renews it when
required, and stores the certificate, chain and (optionally
AES-256-GCM encrypted) private key in a Consul or Redis KV store.

NO exported resources and NO PuppetDB are used. The type is ensurable,
with `exists?` taking into account not only existence but also the
renewal window: a certificate missing from the KV store is issued at
once; one this module issued (its meta document has `acme_renewal`) is
renewed when fewer than `renew_before_days` remain, within the time
window of `renew_schedule`. An entry without `acme_renewal` (written by
another tool) is never overwritten, only reported with a warning. The
meta document's `status` only controls distribution, never renewal.

Writes are protected against concurrent updates via compare-and-set
(Consul: CAS on the ModifyIndex of the meta document; Redis:
WATCH/MULTI/EXEC). If a concurrent write is detected, this run fails
and the next scheduled run retries cleanly.

#### Examples

##### Issue and renew a certificate in Consul (usually declared by acme_kvstore::certificate)

```puppet
acme_kvstore_certificate { 'shop-example-com':
  ensure            => present,
  provider          => 'consul',
  area              => 'web',
  domains           => ['shop.example.com', 'www.shop.example.com'],
  backend_config    => { 'url' => 'https://consul.example.com:8501', 'prefix' => 'acme' },
  area_secret       => $area_secret,
  renew_schedule    => 'nightly',
}
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `acme_kvstore_certificate` type.

##### `ensure`

Valid values: `present`, `absent`

Whether the certificate is kept issued and renewed (`present`), or no longer renewed
(`absent`: removes `acme_renewal` from the meta document; `status` and all versions stay).

Default value: `present`

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `acme_kvstore_certificate` type.

* [`account_email`](#-acme_kvstore_certificate--account_email)
* [`acmesh_path`](#-acme_kvstore_certificate--acmesh_path)
* [`area`](#-acme_kvstore_certificate--area)
* [`area_secret`](#-acme_kvstore_certificate--area_secret)
* [`backend_config`](#-acme_kvstore_certificate--backend_config)
* [`certid`](#-acme_kvstore_certificate--certid)
* [`challenge_alias`](#-acme_kvstore_certificate--challenge_alias)
* [`client_id`](#-acme_kvstore_certificate--client_id)

##### <a name="-acme_kvstore_certificate--account_email"></a>`account_email`

ACME account email registered with the CA (acme.sh --register-account -m). Usually resolved
from a CA profile by acme_kvstore::certificate.

##### <a name="-acme_kvstore_certificate--acmesh_path"></a>`acmesh_path`

Path to the acme.sh executable on the worker host.

Default value: `/root/.acme.sh/acme.sh`

##### <a name="-acme_kvstore_certificate--area"></a>`area`

Logical area for the certificate (determines the KV namespace and area secret).

##### <a name="-acme_kvstore_certificate--area_secret"></a>`area_secret`

32-byte area secret (raw, hex or base64) for AES-256-GCM encryption of the private key.

##### <a name="-acme_kvstore_certificate--backend_config"></a>`backend_config`

Fully resolved backend connection details (Hash), including "prefix". Usually assembled by
acme_kvstore::certificate.

##### <a name="-acme_kvstore_certificate--certid"></a>`certid`

Manually chosen, unique certificate ID (KV path segment).

##### <a name="-acme_kvstore_certificate--challenge_alias"></a>`challenge_alias`

DNS alias mode: the domain whose DNS is actually queried for the _acme-challenge TXT record
(acme.sh --challenge-alias). See docs/profiles.md.

##### <a name="-acme_kvstore_certificate--client_id"></a>`client_id`

Value of the 'client' field in the stored JSON documents. Usually resolved from
$acme_kvstore::kv_client by acme_kvstore::certificate.

Default value: `puppet`

##### <a name="-acme_kvstore_certificate--dns_env"></a>`dns_env`

Environment variables (Hash of NAME => value), set before invoking acme.sh (DNS API credentials).

Default value: `{}`

##### <a name="-acme_kvstore_certificate--dns_options"></a>`dns_options`

Additional hook-specific options (Hash). The 'dnssleep' key becomes the --dnssleep CLI flag;
every other key becomes an upper-cased environment variable for the DNS hook.

Default value: `{}`

##### <a name="-acme_kvstore_certificate--dns_provider"></a>`dns_provider`

acme.sh DNS API hook name (e.g. 'dns_cf') for DNS-01 validation. If unset, --webroot is used.
Usually resolved from a DNS profile by acme_kvstore::certificate.

##### <a name="-acme_kvstore_certificate--dnssleep"></a>`dnssleep`

DNS-01 only: seconds acme.sh waits for the TXT records to propagate (acme.sh --dnssleep).
Always passed, so acme.sh never polls public DNS-over-HTTPS resolvers itself.

Default value: `60`

##### <a name="-acme_kvstore_certificate--domain_alias"></a>`domain_alias`

DNS alias mode: the domain alias used for validation (acme.sh --domain-alias). See docs/profiles.md.

##### <a name="-acme_kvstore_certificate--domains"></a>`domains`

The primary domain (CN) first, then any further names. Usually built by
acme_kvstore::certificate from its domain and subject_alt_names.

##### <a name="-acme_kvstore_certificate--eab_hmac_key"></a>`eab_hmac_key`

External Account Binding HMAC key, paired with eab_kid.

##### <a name="-acme_kvstore_certificate--eab_kid"></a>`eab_kid`

External Account Binding key ID, required by some CAs (e.g. ZeroSSL, SSL.com, Google Public CA).

##### <a name="-acme_kvstore_certificate--exec_timeout"></a>`exec_timeout`

Maximum time in seconds any single acme.sh invocation (including account registration and any
posthook_cmd) may run before being terminated. Should be higher than any configured dnssleep.

Default value: `300`

##### <a name="-acme_kvstore_certificate--key_size"></a>`key_size`

RSA key length in bits, or EC curve (256/384) when key_type = ec.

Default value: `2048`

##### <a name="-acme_kvstore_certificate--key_type"></a>`key_type`

Valid values: `rsa`, `ec`

Private key algorithm, passed through to acme.sh.

Default value: `rsa`

##### <a name="-acme_kvstore_certificate--log_file"></a>`log_file`

acme.sh log file (acme.sh --log). No log file is written when unset. Usually resolved from
acme_kvstore::worker's acme_log_file by acme_kvstore::certificate.

##### <a name="-acme_kvstore_certificate--log_level"></a>`log_level`

Valid values: `1`, `2`, `1`, `2`

acme.sh log level (acme.sh --log-level): 1 (normal) or 2 (debug). Only used together with log_file.

Default value: `1`

##### <a name="-acme_kvstore_certificate--posthook_cmd"></a>`posthook_cmd`

An optional command run after a certificate has been successfully issued/renewed and stored.
Runs on the ACME worker, which does not necessarily serve the certificate itself in this
module's architecture - typical uses are notifying an external system or triggering
redistribution to consumer nodes. Failure is logged but never fails the resource, since the
certificate has already been issued and stored successfully by that point. See
docs/profiles.md.

##### <a name="-acme_kvstore_certificate--prefix"></a>`prefix`

Overrides the global KV prefix ($acme_kvstore::prefix) for this certificate.

##### <a name="-acme_kvstore_certificate--provider"></a>`provider`

The specific backend to use for this `acme_kvstore_certificate` resource. You will seldom need to specify this ---
Puppet will usually discover the appropriate provider for your platform.

##### <a name="-acme_kvstore_certificate--proxy"></a>`proxy`

HTTP(S) proxy used for all of acme.sh's outbound connections (to the ACME CA and any DNS API),
e.g. 'proxy.example.com:3128' or a full URL. acme.sh has no dedicated CLI flag for this; it is
implemented via the standard HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY environment variables.

##### <a name="-acme_kvstore_certificate--purge_key_on_mismatch"></a>`purge_key_on_mismatch`

Valid values: `true`, `false`

Whether a changed key_type/key_size forces an immediate reissue with a new key (true, the
default). With false, the new key settings only take effect at the next regular renewal. A
changed domains list always forces an immediate reissue.

Default value: `true`

##### <a name="-acme_kvstore_certificate--renew_before_days"></a>`renew_before_days`

The certificate is considered due for renewal when fewer than this many days remain until expiry.

Default value: `30`

##### <a name="-acme_kvstore_certificate--renew_schedule"></a>`renew_schedule`

Name of a `schedule` resource whose `range` and `weekday` limit when a due renewal may run
(`period`/`repeat` are ignored). First issuance and configuration changes are not limited.
Unset: any time.

##### <a name="-acme_kvstore_certificate--run_as_group"></a>`run_as_group`

Run acme.sh (and posthook_cmd) as this group. Accepts a group name or a numeric GID. Usually
resolved from acme_kvstore::worker by acme_kvstore::certificate.

##### <a name="-acme_kvstore_certificate--run_as_home"></a>`run_as_home`

The HOME directory to use for the run_as_user account, so acme.sh finds its own account/config
data. Usually resolved from acme_kvstore::worker by acme_kvstore::certificate.

##### <a name="-acme_kvstore_certificate--run_as_user"></a>`run_as_user`

Run acme.sh (and posthook_cmd) as this user instead of the Puppet agent's own user (usually
root). Accepts a username or a numeric UID. Usually resolved from acme_kvstore::worker by
acme_kvstore::certificate.

##### <a name="-acme_kvstore_certificate--server"></a>`server`

ACME server/CA, passed through to acme.sh --server (e.g. 'letsencrypt', 'zerossl', or a URL).
Usually resolved from a CA profile by acme_kvstore::certificate.

Default value: `letsencrypt`

##### <a name="-acme_kvstore_certificate--store_issuers"></a>`store_issuers`

Valid values: `true`, `false`

Whether to store each certificate of the chain acme.sh returns as an issuer entry of its own
(certid = <cn>_<expiry date>, e.g. r11_2027-03-12) and record them in acme_renewal. With false, readers find the
chain among the certificates already in the area (e.g. maintained in CCI-UI).

Default value: `true`

##### <a name="-acme_kvstore_certificate--tags"></a>`tags`

Free-form tags stored in the certificate document.

Default value: `[]`

##### <a name="-acme_kvstore_certificate--updated_by"></a>`updated_by`

Value of the 'updated_by' / 'created_by' fields. Defaults to this node's certname; usually
resolved from $acme_kvstore::kv_updated_by or the worker's FQDN by acme_kvstore::certificate.

##### <a name="-acme_kvstore_certificate--webroot"></a>`webroot`

HTTP-01 only: webroot directory acme.sh writes the challenge files to (acme.sh --webroot).
Usually resolved from acme_kvstore::worker's webroot by acme_kvstore::certificate.

Default value: `/var/www/acme-challenge`

## Functions

### <a name="acme_kvstore--lookup_cert"></a>`acme_kvstore::lookup_cert`

Type: Ruby 4.x API

Reads directly from Consul/Redis while the catalogue is compiled, for
delivering a certificate to any node (see docs/lookup_cert.md).
Certificate and key data are only returned while the status is
'active'.

#### Examples

##### Deliver an active certificate's PEM and key to a node's catalog

```puppet
$cert = acme_kvstore::lookup_cert('shop-example-com', 'web', 'consul',
  { 'url' => 'https://consul.example.com:8501', 'prefix' => 'acme' }, $area_secret, true)
if $cert['status'] == 'active' {
  file { '/etc/ssl/certs/shop.pem': content => $cert['pem'] }
  file { '/etc/ssl/private/shop.key': content => Sensitive($cert['private_key']), mode => '0600' }
}
```

#### `acme_kvstore::lookup_cert(String[1] $certid, String[1] $area, Enum[consul, redis] $backend, Hash $backend_config, Optional[Optional[String[1]]] $area_secret, Optional[Boolean] $decrypt_key, Optional[Boolean] $include_chain, Optional[Boolean] $include_root)`

Reads directly from Consul/Redis while the catalogue is compiled, for
delivering a certificate to any node (see docs/lookup_cert.md).
Certificate and key data are only returned while the status is
'active'.

Returns: `Hash` A Hash with the keys 'status', 'active_version', 'latest_version', 'updated_at', 'pem' (certificate only),
with include_chain 'chain' (issuers without self-signed roots, built from the issuer entries), 'fullchain'
(certificate + chain), 'chain_missing' (the certificate's issuer is not stored; chain/fullchain are then undef),
'chain_error' (why the issuer search failed, if it did), 'root' (the self-signed root of the chain, if stored;
never part of chain/fullchain),
'has_key', 'private_key'.

##### Examples

###### Deliver an active certificate's PEM and key to a node's catalog

```puppet
$cert = acme_kvstore::lookup_cert('shop-example-com', 'web', 'consul',
  { 'url' => 'https://consul.example.com:8501', 'prefix' => 'acme' }, $area_secret, true)
if $cert['status'] == 'active' {
  file { '/etc/ssl/certs/shop.pem': content => $cert['pem'] }
  file { '/etc/ssl/private/shop.key': content => Sensitive($cert['private_key']), mode => '0600' }
}
```

##### `certid`

Data type: `String[1]`

The certificate ID to look up.

##### `area`

Data type: `String[1]`

The area the certificate belongs to.

##### `backend`

Data type: `Enum[consul, redis]`

Which KV backend to query: 'consul' or 'redis'.

##### `backend_config`

Data type: `Hash`

Backend connection details (Hash), including 'prefix' - see docs/consul.md / docs/redis.md.

##### `area_secret`

Data type: `Optional[Optional[String[1]]]`

The area's 32-byte secret. Required only when decrypt_key is true.

##### `decrypt_key`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Whether to also decrypt and return the private key. Defaults to false.

##### `include_chain`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Whether to build the chain (chain, fullchain, root) at all; it can cost a read of all certificates
of the area. Defaults to false.

##### `include_root`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

With include_chain: whether to also search the area for the root if the recorded chain does not end in
one. Defaults to false.

### <a name="acme_kvstore--request_cert"></a>`acme_kvstore::request_cert`

Type: Ruby 4.x API

For manual testing on the ACME worker, e.g.
`puppet apply -e "notice(acme_kvstore::request_cert(['example.com']))"`.

#### `acme_kvstore::request_cert(Array[String[1]] $domains, Optional[Hash] $options)`

For manual testing on the ACME worker, e.g.
`puppet apply -e "notice(acme_kvstore::request_cert(['example.com']))"`.

Returns: `Hash` Hash with the keys 'cert', 'chain', 'fullchain', 'key' (PEM strings or undef).

##### `domains`

Data type: `Array[String[1]]`

Primary domain plus any SANs.

##### `options`

Data type: `Optional[Hash]`

Optional settings: key_type, key_size, server, dns_provider, dns_env, dns_options,
challenge_alias, domain_alias, account_email, eab_kid, eab_hmac_key, proxy,
exec_timeout, run_as_user, run_as_group, run_as_home, acmesh_path, dnssleep (default 60), webroot,
log_file, log_level.

## Data types

### <a name="Acme_kvstore--Area"></a>`Acme_kvstore::Area`

Each area has its own 32-byte AES secret (raw, hex or base64) and its own
KV credentials, limited to the area's keys below <prefix>/<area>/:
- for the ACME worker (read/write): consul_token with Consul,
  redis_username/redis_password with Redis (required by the acme_kvstore
  class for the backend in use);
- for acme_kvstore::deploy (read only): consul_read_token, or
  redis_read_username/redis_read_password (required by deploy when it
  builds the connection from Hiera).

Alias of

```puppet
Struct[{
  secret                          => Acme_kvstore::Secret,
  Optional['consul_token']        => Acme_kvstore::Secret,
  Optional['redis_username']      => String[1],
  Optional['redis_password']      => Acme_kvstore::Secret,
  Optional['consul_read_token']   => Acme_kvstore::Secret,
  Optional['redis_read_username'] => String[1],
  Optional['redis_read_password'] => Acme_kvstore::Secret,
}]
```

### <a name="Acme_kvstore--Area_name"></a>`Acme_kvstore::Area_name`

The name of an area, as CCI-UI accepts it: [a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,47}.

Alias of `Pattern[/\A[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,47}\z/]`

### <a name="Acme_kvstore--Ca_profile"></a>`Acme_kvstore::Ca_profile`

directory_url is omitted for acme.sh's built-in CA aliases (the profile
name is used instead). See docs/profiles.md.

Alias of

```puppet
Struct[{
  Optional['directory_url'] => Stdlib::HTTPSUrl,
  Optional['account_email'] => String[1],
  Optional['eab_kid']       => Acme_kvstore::Secret,
  Optional['eab_hmac_key']  => Acme_kvstore::Secret,
}]
```

### <a name="Acme_kvstore--Certid"></a>`Acme_kvstore::Certid`

A certificate ID: a single KV path segment (letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-'),
at most 120 characters as in CCI-UI.

Alias of `Pattern[/\A[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,120}\z/]`

### <a name="Acme_kvstore--Certificate_params"></a>`Acme_kvstore::Certificate_params`

The key of the entry is the certid. Only domain is required; everything
else defaults as in acme_kvstore::certificate. Keep in sync with that
defined type (spec/type_aliases/acme_kvstore__certificate_params_spec.rb checks).

Alias of

```puppet
Struct[{
  domain                            => Acme_kvstore::Domain,
  Optional['subject_alt_names']     => Array[Acme_kvstore::Domain],
  Optional['area']                  => String[1],
  Optional['worker']                => Stdlib::Fqdn,
  Optional['backend']               => Enum['consul', 'redis'],
  Optional['key_type']              => Enum['rsa', 'ec'],
  Optional['key_size']              => Integer[256],
  Optional['renew_before_days']     => Integer[1],
  Optional['purge_key_on_mismatch'] => Boolean,
  Optional['store_issuers']         => Boolean,
  Optional['tags']                  => Array[String[1]],
  Optional['challenge_type']        => Enum['http-01', 'dns-01'],
  Optional['use_dns_profile']       => String[1],
  Optional['dns_provider']          => Pattern[/\Adns_[a-z0-9_]+\z/],
  Optional['dns_env']               => Hash[String[1], String[1]],
  Optional['challenge_alias']       => Stdlib::Fqdn,
  Optional['domain_alias']          => Stdlib::Fqdn,
  Optional['dnssleep']              => Integer[1],
  Optional['use_ca_profile']        => String[1],
  Optional['posthook_cmd']          => String[1],
  Optional['proxy']                 => String[1],
  Optional['exec_timeout']          => Integer[1],
  Optional['renew_schedule']        => String[1],
}]
```

### <a name="Acme_kvstore--Consul_config"></a>`Acme_kvstore::Consul_config`

Deliberately without a 'token': every area uses its own consul_token
(see Acme_kvstore::Area), so a token with access to all areas cannot be
configured here. The KV prefix is added from $acme_kvstore::prefix.

Alias of

```puppet
Struct[{
  Optional['url']          => Stdlib::HTTPUrl,
  Optional['datacenter']   => String[1],
  Optional['ca_file']      => Stdlib::Absolutepath,
  Optional['cert_file']    => Stdlib::Absolutepath,
  Optional['key_file']     => Stdlib::Absolutepath,
  Optional['insecure']     => Boolean,
  Optional['read_timeout'] => Integer[1],
}]
```

### <a name="Acme_kvstore--Dh_param_size"></a>`Acme_kvstore::Dh_param_size`

Size of the RFC 7919 ffdhe group used for DH parameters (see acme_kvstore::deploy).

Alias of `Variant[Integer[2048, 2048], Integer[3072, 3072], Integer[4096, 4096]]`

### <a name="Acme_kvstore--Dns_profile"></a>`Acme_kvstore::Dns_profile`

hook is the full acme.sh DNS API hook name ('dns_aws', 'dns_cf', ...);
every hook shipped with acme.sh follows that naming. A hook acme.sh does
not ship needs a script in $acme_kvstore::dnsapi_scripts. See docs/profiles.md.

Alias of

```puppet
Struct[{
  hook                        => Pattern[/\Adns_[a-z0-9_]+\z/],
  Optional['env']             => Hash[String[1], Acme_kvstore::Secret],
  Optional['options']         => Hash[String[1], Variant[String[1], Integer, Sensitive[String[1]]]],
  Optional['challenge_alias'] => Stdlib::Fqdn,
  Optional['domain_alias']    => Stdlib::Fqdn,
}]
```

### <a name="Acme_kvstore--Dnsapi_script"></a>`Acme_kvstore::Dnsapi_script`

Exactly one of source (puppet:/// URL or absolute path) or content. The
script defines <hook>_add/<hook>_rm; DNS profiles use it via their hook.
See docs/profiles.md.

Alias of `Variant[Struct[{ source => Stdlib::Filesource }], Struct[{ content => String[1] }]]`

### <a name="Acme_kvstore--Domain"></a>`Acme_kvstore::Domain`

A domain name for a certificate: an FQDN or a wildcard name ('*.example.com').

Alias of `Variant[Stdlib::Fqdn, Pattern[/\A\*\.(([a-zA-Z0-9]|[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9-]*[a-zA-Z0-9])\.)*([a-zA-Z0-9]|[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9-]*[a-zA-Z0-9])\z/]]`

### <a name="Acme_kvstore--Redis_config"></a>`Acme_kvstore::Redis_config`

Deliberately without 'username'/'password': every area authenticates as
its own Redis ACL user (redis_username/redis_password, see
Acme_kvstore::Area). The KV prefix is added from $acme_kvstore::prefix.

Alias of

```puppet
Struct[{
  Optional['host']      => Stdlib::Host,
  Optional['port']      => Stdlib::Port,
  Optional['db']        => Integer[0],
  Optional['tls']       => Boolean,
  Optional['ca_file']   => Stdlib::Absolutepath,
  Optional['cert_file'] => Stdlib::Absolutepath,
  Optional['key_file']  => Stdlib::Absolutepath,
  Optional['insecure']  => Boolean,
}]
```

### <a name="Acme_kvstore--Secret"></a>`Acme_kvstore::Secret`

A secret value, as a plain String (e.g. already protected by hiera-eyaml) or wrapped in Sensitive for redaction.

Alias of `Variant[String[1], Sensitive[String[1]]]`
